title: The Inductance Bench
summary: Find self- and mutual inductance, solenoid energy and the energy density of a magnetic field.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can use self- and mutual inductance to find emfs and flux linkage, find the inductance and stored energy of a solenoid, and find the energy density of a magnetic field.

levels.title: Self-inductance
levels.adds: Baseline: the emf of self-induction is L ΔI/Δt, used both ways round (Ex 6.7).
hints: To find L, multiply the emf by Δt and divide by ΔI.
The emf opposes the change in current.

levels.title: Mutual inductance
levels.adds: New idea: flux linkage in one coil is M times the current in the other (Ex 6.8).
hints: The flux linkage is M I, so its change is M ΔI.
The emf is the change in flux linkage divided by the time.
Keep the units: henry times ampere is weber.

levels.title: Solenoid and energy
levels.adds: New idea: L = μ₀N²A/l and the energy stored is ½LI² (Section 6.7.2).
hints: Convert the area to m² and the length to metres.
L = μ₀N²A/l, in henry; convert to mH.

levels.title: Concentric coils
levels.adds: More steps: use the field at the centre of the large coil to find the mutual inductance (Example 6.8).
hints: The large coil gives B = μ₀N₂I₂/2r₂ at the centre.
The small coil sees that field over its area πr₁² with N₁ turns.
M is the flux linkage per unit current.

levels.title: Energy in a field
levels.adds: Apply it: the energy per unit volume in a magnetic field is B²/2μ₀ (Example 6.9).
hints: u = B²/2μ₀, in joules per cubic metre.
Convert the volume from cm³ to m³.

misconceptions: The emf of self-induction depends on the size of the current, not its rate of change
The stored energy in an inductor is LI²
Inductance depends on the current in the coil
